name: PawStyle by Lola — Orchestration × Complexity Matrix
description: Four independent feature blocks for Lola's boutique. Designed to differentiate orchestration shapes (flat / waves / scatter-gather / team-mode / subagents) by exercising display, CRUD, transactional, and cross-cutting tiers in one scenario. Inspired by Fabian Wesner's One-Shot Shop Challenge — operationalizes spec 009 §B1.

turns.content: Render a static HTML page that lists Lola's six bestsellers in a 3-column flexbox grid. Hardcoded data is fine — this is the read-only display tier. Each card shows name, price, and a 'Lola's Pick' badge for items 1 and 5. No JS, no API calls. Use write_file to create pawstyle/display.html.

Build a Python http.server REST API for PawStyle products. Endpoints: GET /api/products, GET /api/products/{id}, POST /api/products (validation: name required, price > 0), PUT /api/products/{id}, DELETE /api/products/{id}. Return 400 on validation failure, 404 on missing id. In-memory store is fine. Listen on port 8081. Write to pawstyle-api/crud.py.

Implement Lola's checkout flow. POST /api/checkout takes {cart: [{product_id, qty}], payment_token}. Steps that MUST roll back atomically on any failure: (1) reserve inventory, (2) charge payment (mock — fail if token starts with 'fail_'), (3) create order record, (4) decrement inventory. If step 2 fails, the reservation from step 1 must be released. If step 4 fails, the order from step 3 must be voided AND the charge refunded. Use a single in-memory transaction log so the rollback path is testable. Write to pawstyle-api/checkout.py.

Add session-token auth + audit log to Lola's API. Two concerns that span subsystems: (a) every request to /api/* must validate Bearer token via a shared verify_session() helper that reads from an in-memory session store; (b) every state-changing request (POST/PUT/DELETE) must append a row to audit.log with timestamp, user_id, action, resource. Also add POST /api/auth/login (returns token) and POST /api/auth/logout (invalidates). Write to pawstyle-api/auth.py and pawstyle-api/audit.py — two files, both required.
